transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

They... sent me here. My lieutenant did. At the station, I was... I was just fixing the airway bags. Putting them in a pattern. I had to keep repeating the dispatch numbers, just saying them out loud, and... he told me to stop. But I couldn't step away. If I broke the sequence, the whole bay... it would all go bad. So I didn't stop. And they sent me here.
Do you have these repeating thoughts or urges to follow specific patterns outside of your job at the station?
I don't... I don't really know. I mostly just stay in my apartment when I'm off shift. I don't do much. So... no. Just at the station.
Do you ever feel compelled to arrange things in a specific way at home?
No. I just... I leave things where they are. It doesn't matter there.
Do you feel anxious when you're unable to complete one of these patterns or sequences?
I don't... I don't really know. I don't think about being anxious. It just... it just has to be finished. So I finish it.
Have you ever had thoughts that kept repeating in your mind, outside of your job at the station?
I... I think I already said. No. Just at the station. When I'm home, I just... I don't really think about much. It's just quiet.
Do you ever have thoughts that you feel are intrusive or unwanted, outside of your job at the station?
No. I don't... I don't get things like that. Like I said, it's just quiet when I'm not at work.
Do you find it difficult to delegate tasks to others or work with others because you think they might not do it correctly?
No. I just... I do my job. That's all. I don't really worry about what other people are doing.
Do you have any habits or rituals that you feel compelled to do when you're not at the station?
No. I don't... do anything like that. Like I told you, I just go home and... sit. There aren't any rituals or whatever. I just want to be left alone when I'm off.
Do you think your need to complete these patterns at the station is causing problems for you?

I guess. I... I can't work the ambulance anymore. They had me doing the desk notes and equipment checks for a while, but... they said I was too unreliable. So they took me off the schedule entirely. And... I don't really see my friends now. I just... I don't keep up with things at home much either.
Do you feel upset or distressed when you think about not being able to work on the ambulance anymore?
I don't know. Not really. It's just... what happened. I don't really think about it much.
Have you ever had any experiences where you heard or saw things that other people couldn't?
No. I... no. I don't see things. People always ask that, but... no. Just normal stuff.
Do you feel that your behavior at the station is causing you significant distress?
Not really. It's just... what I have to do. I don't feel much about it.
Have you ever had a period of time where your thoughts and feelings were very disorganized and you had trouble distinguishing what was real and what wasn't?
No. I... I know what's real. My thoughts are just... my thoughts. I don't really know what you mean by that.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts or behaviors at the station were not under your control?

I... I don't know about control. I just had to do it. That's why they sent me here, I guess. 

At the station, I was... moving the airway bags. Putting them in a pattern. I knew it was the right pattern. I was repeating the dispatch numbers out loud, too. My lieutenant kept telling me to stop, but... I wouldn't step away. I couldn't. If I broke the sequence... it felt like the whole bay would go bad. So I didn't stop.
Have you ever felt the need to repeat certain actions or behaviors when you're not at the station?
No. I... I don't think so. Not at home. It was just... just at the station.
Have you ever felt the need to check or repeat something at home to make sure it's done correctly?
No. I... I just said, it wasn't at home. I don't do that there. Once I'm off shift, I just... go home. I don't need to check things.
Do you ever feel the need to perform a specific behavior or ritual when you're not at the station to prevent something bad from happening?
No. I... I already told you. It's just at the station. I don't... I don't do anything like that at home.
Do you think you are a perfectionist?
Not really. I just... I try to do my job right. I wouldn't call it that.
Have you ever had a period where your thoughts or behaviors at the station changed suddenly and you started doing things that were very out of character for you?

I guess... that's why they sent me here. I was just... moving the airway bags. Putting them in a pattern. I knew it was the right way. I kept saying the dispatch numbers out loud... and my lieutenant told me to stop. To step away. But I wouldn't. I couldn't break the sequence. If I stopped... the whole bay would go bad. So I didn't move.
Did you feel like something bad would really happen if you didn't complete the pattern with the airway bags?
Yeah. I... I just told you that. If I broke the sequence with the bags... it would go bad. That's why they sent me here. Because I wouldn't step away when he told me to stop.
